principles: Host-neutral research control belongs in deterministic artifacts, not Codex- or Claude-specific prompts.
Do not optimize for the sake of optimization; freeze only launch inputs needed to prevent invalid comparisons.
Only fix real correctness issues: required cell ② must be represented, optional ④ must not masquerade as required.
Consistency of logic: M1 can block Phase 1, but must not claim Phase 1 outcomes.
Provider-costing execution requires explicit later approval and dated snapshots.
drivers: Phase 1 comparisons are only meaningful if protocol digest, seed rules, cells, and budget sequencing are frozen first.
The user wants visible milestone progress without accidentally spending provider budget.
The checklist must encode the repaired requirement that ③, ⑥, and ② are required while ④ is optional.

options.name: deterministic-m1-lock-artifacts-with-local-checker
pros: Creates machine-checkable launch boundaries before provider execution.
Keeps M1 provider-free and repeatable across hosts.
Can reject drift, missing required ②, illegal ② vs ④ confirmatory comparison, and premature launchAllowed=true.
cons: Does not produce experimental outcome data by itself.
Requires a later explicit M2 campaign approval to answer model-family questions.

options.name: run-phase1-immediately
pros: Would produce data sooner if all launch inputs were already locked.
cons: Burns provider budget before human approval and before dated snapshot/task/budget locks are complete.
Risks invalid comparisons if required ② or A2prime budget sequencing drifts.

options.name: prose-only-status-note
cons: Does not give a mechanical launch gate or negative controls.
Would let later agents overclaim readiness from stale prose.

rationale: This is the smallest correctness-preserving step: it freezes M1 launch inputs and blocks invalid Phase 1 execution without spending provider budget or inventing outcome claims.

preMortem.scenario: The M1 matrix omits required cell ② but still appears launch-ready.
preMortem.trigger: Treating ② and ④ as optional together instead of only making ④ optional.
preMortem.consequence: Phase 1 cannot answer the E1 fixed-executor cross-review direction and later analysis is underpowered or misleading.
preMortem.mitigation: Encode ③, ⑥, and ② as required in the matrix and checker; allow only ④ to be absent as budget-permitting.

preMortem.scenario: A later agent treats M1 DONE as permission to run providers.
preMortem.trigger: launchAllowed or providerCallEnabled accidentally set true in M1 artifacts.
preMortem.consequence: Cost-bearing runs happen without explicit approval or dated snapshots.
preMortem.mitigation: Make launchAllowed=false and providerCallEnabled=false required assertions and add negative controls for premature true values.

preMortem.scenario: A2prime rows are run before same-family A4 budget calibration.
preMortem.trigger: Seed/cell manifests do not express A4-before-A2prime sequencing.
preMortem.consequence: Budget lock can be backfilled after seeing outcomes, invalidating comparisons.
preMortem.mitigation: Represent A2prime sequencing blockers and reject A2prime execution readiness without budgetLockSource=cell-③/A4 calibration.

preMortem.scenario: The checker becomes paper theater and misses illegal causal contrasts.
preMortem.trigger: It only validates file presence, not comparison semantics.
preMortem.consequence: ② vs ④ could be reported as confirmatory despite both executor and reviewer varying.
preMortem.mitigation: Assert legal confirmatory comparisons explicitly and reject ② vs ④ as confirmatory in negative controls.
